players.product: US utility (Georgia Power) - transformer buyer (HICO America customer)

quarterly_data.signal: Southern Company's 10-K: total estimated capital expenditures, primarily at the traditional electric operating companies, rose from $45.2 billion previously estimated for 2024 through 2028 to $78.1 billion currently estimated for 2026 through 2030, as those companies project a significant increase in electricity demand largely driven by data centers and other large load customers. Through the 2022 IRP and 2023 IRP Update the Georgia PSC certified approximately 13 GWs of resources, approximately nine GWs of which are new generation and battery energy storage facilities being built by Georgia Power at a certified cost of $19.5 billion, projected to be placed in service through 2030.
quarterly_data.figure: capex plan $78.1 billion (2026-2030) vs $45.2 billion (2024-2028); ~13 GWs certified, ~nine GWs Georgia Power new generation/storage at $19.5 billion through 2030
